links.title: Chapter 18 - CSV, JSON, and XML Files, Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 3rd Ed
links.why: The course textbook's own chapter, free online: csv, json, ElementTree, Project 13 and the practice questions.

links.title: csv — CSV File Reading and Writing — Python 3.14.8 documentation
links.why: Every reader and writer option: dialects, quoting modes, DictReader and DictWriter, line_num and the newline='' rule.

links.title: json — JSON encoder and decoder — Python 3.14.8 documentation
links.why: loads, dumps, load and dump with their options, the types that convert and the errors raised.

links.title: xml.etree.ElementTree — The ElementTree XML API — Python 3.14.8 documentation
links.why: Parsing, finding, building and writing XML, the XPath subset, iterparse and the Element truth-value warning.

links.title: XML Processing Modules — Python 3.14.8 documentation
links.why: The modules of the xml package and the table of attacks (entity expansion, external entities) each one is open to.

links.title: tomllib — Parse TOML files — Python 3.14.8 documentation
links.why: Reading TOML, the conversion table, and the fact that the module can read but not write.

links.title: io — Core tools for working with streams — Python 3.14.8 documentation
links.why: StringIO, BytesIO and TextIOWrapper: the newline argument and what it does to line ends.

links.title: RFC 4180: Common Format and MIME Type for Comma-Separated Values (CSV) Files | RFC Editor
links.why: The informal definition of CSV: CRLF line breaks, quoting of commas, quotes and line breaks, and the optional header line.

links.title: RFC 8259: The JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Data Interchange Format | RFC Editor
links.why: The six value types, the text rules and why a trailing comma is not JSON.

links.title: Billion laughs attack - Wikipedia
links.why: The attack by nested entities, its other names and the entry in the CVE list.

links.title: defusedxml · PyPI
links.why: The package that refuses entities, external references and DTDs in XML from an untrusted source.

links.title: openpyxl - A Python library to read/write Excel 2010 xlsx/xlsm files — openpyxl 3.1.3 documentation
links.why: Reading the cells of a workbook, the Excel-to-CSV converter's first step.

_note: Every url was opened with an HTTP download on the date in 'checked' (all answered 200) and its page title read; the titles are those the pages served (the Python documentation was headed 3.14.8 and the openpyxl documentation 3.1.3, while the research ran Python 3.14.6 and openpyxl 3.1.5). The concept named for each link is a concept of this page. No video or discussion thread is listed: none was opened and read, so the page offers labelled searches instead and the course owner may add checked ones here.
